name_note: The GTDB name carries the suffix _I because Eubacterium as classically defined is split into several GTDB genera; the literature calls this organism Eubacterium ramulus.

sentences.text: Eubacterium ramulus is a human intestinal anaerobe known for its ability to degrade various dietary flavonoids.
It can degrade quercetin, one of the most commonly consumed flavonoids, in the presence of glucose, but cannot use starch for growth or quercetin degradation.

A study reported that the starch-metabolising Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron stimulates quercetin degradation and butyrate production by Eubacterium ramulus through cross-feeding of glucose and maltose.
Culture experiments reported that Eubacterium ramulus hydrogenates xanthohumol, a prenylated flavonoid of hops and beer, and converts the phytoestrogen 8-prenylnaringenin into chalcones.
An oxygen-sensitive NADH-dependent reductase purified from Eubacterium ramulus cleaves the heterocyclic C-ring of flavanones and flavanonols.
